```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("R/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_small <- simulate_bdat602(n = 10000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1 — Fit PCA pipeline

```{r task1}
library(recipes)
library(dplyr)

pca_vars <- c("age", "bmi", "income", "num_claims",
              "claim_amount", "num_chronic_conditions")

pca_rec <- recipe(~ ., data = health_small[, pca_vars]) |>
  step_impute_median(bmi, income) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_pca(all_numeric_predictors(), num_comp = 3)

pca_prep   <- prep(pca_rec)
pca_scores <- bake(pca_prep, new_data = NULL)

head(pca_scores)
```

## Task 2 — Scree plot

```{r task2}
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)

tidy(pca_prep, number = 3, type = "variance") |>
  filter(terms == "percent variance") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = component, y = value)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(group = 1, colour = "red") +
  geom_point(colour = "red") +
  labs(title = "Scree Plot: PCA on Health Insurance Variables",
       x = "Principal Component", y = "% Variance Explained") +
  theme_minimal()
```

PC1 typically explains ~30–40% of variance (capturing the utilisation/cost dimension), PC2 ~20% (capturing premium/income), and PC3 ~15%.

## Task 3 — Score plot coloured by plan_tier

```{r task3}
plan <- health_small |>
  select(bmi, income, num_chronic_conditions, plan_tier) |>
  mutate(
    bmi    = if_else(is.na(bmi),    median(bmi,    na.rm = TRUE), bmi),
    income = if_else(is.na(income), median(income, na.rm = TRUE), income)
  ) |>
  na.omit() |>
  pull(plan_tier)

pca_scores |>
  mutate(plan_tier = plan) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = plan_tier)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "PCA Score Plot by Plan Tier",
       colour = "Plan Tier") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Platinum and Gold policyholders should separate along PC1 (higher utilisation) and PC2 (higher income/premium), while Bronze clusters at lower PC1 scores.
